name: Bublinki
beta: Follow a crack up to the horizontal break, then continue on the face past a pair of bolts.
overview: Begins around the corner from Top-Topic on the same tower, combining a crack with face climbing protected by two bolts.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: around to the right of Top-Topic

name: Space Metal
beta: Three bolts lead to a ledge on the tower's east side, and the higher section of that side is then climbed with two more bolts.
overview: Bolted climbing to the tower eastern ledge, then continues up the higher eastern face.

current.location: below and right of I Slept With L.K.

name: Top Topic
beta: On the southwest face, work leftward up a flake and ledge system, then continue past a horizontal break and a single bolt to the summit.
overview: Goes up and left along a flake and ledge, then past a horizontal break and a bolt to the summit.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: southwest face of South Frolic Tower

name: Young in Deed
beta: A direct line up the face with two bolts leads to the belay of Twinkle Toes. Beginning instead at the start of the Twinkle Toes traverse makes the lead safer.
overview: A short, bolted face climb that begins beneath a neighboring route's first belay and joins it. The R in its rating marks the lead as serious.

current.area_walk_in: From the west side parking lot, walk about 0.6 miles up the Balconies Trail to its junction with the Balconies Caves Trail. Then follow the marked climbers' path, signed with a carabiner symbol, up to the base. Stay on it, since the vegetation alongside is being restored.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: right below where Twinkle Toes Traverse's first pitch ends

name: Balconies- Regular Route
beta: Low on the route, beware a big loose block, and treat the bolt ladder with suspicion since the bolts are in poor shape.
overview: A historic line that was first to climb the principal eastern wall, once seen as a hard aid route. Even free, it is still demanding, with loose rock, aging bolts and a corner system coated in guano.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: East-facing main wall of the cliff, the first line to climb it

name: Bongloadash
beta: Medium to large cams in the lower chimney make the opening safer; higher, four bolts take you to the top.
overview: A frightening, crumbly line in a black waterchute at the far left end of the Balconies, starting in a chimney and then continuing up with bolts above it.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: black waterchute just left of the chimney that begins the Balconies

name: Echoes
beta: Climb the wall below the biggest chockstone clipping two bolts, then exit through the big opening at mid-height and clip three more bolts to a belay with two bolts.
overview: Takes the face under the biggest chockstone in the gully, then exits through the large gap about halfway up. It also works as a lead-in up into the Nexus Area and avoids the poison oak.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: wall under the biggest chockstone in the gully corridor

name: Bar Fight
beta: Follows the line of bolts directly upward along the rock's right-hand edge, then eases off by trending leftward onto easier ground.
overview: Runs straight up the line of bolts on the rock's right-hand side before easing off onto gentler ground toward the left.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.anchor: pair of bolts, same station as Bar Fly
current.location: right side of the rock

name: Bar Fly
beta: Begin in the corner and drift slightly rightward, eventually mounting a chunkier face. Expect technical climbing with six bolts along the way.
overview: A technical, well-rated sport line that starts in a corner and ends on a blockier face. It shares its anchors with Bar Fight.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: starts in a corner and angles slightly right onto blockier face

name: Bat Crack
beta: Start up a curving chimney that leads to a ledge equipped with rappel anchors (Bat Ledge), then follow the obvious crack overhead.
overview: A curving chimney gives access to a slanting terrace, and a clear-cut crack continues higher.

current.anchor: rappel anchors at the ledge partway up
current.location: 20 ft right of where Billabong starts

name: Bats with Aids (aka Woof Woof)
beta: Climb to the first bolt, shuffle left along a horizontal crack, then continue up past a second bolt. How hard it feels depends on your height.
overview: A short face line on the northwest face's right-hand portion, around the corner from a neighbor. It links two bolts by way of a horizontal crack; how hard it feels depends on height.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Beak of the Week
beta: Climbs the boulder's east arete, starting from a neighboring boulder, with a lone bolt around mid-height.
overview: Climbs the boulder's eastern edge with a single bolt about midway.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: east arete of a big boulder below and right of the beak feature, started from a neighbouring boulder

name: Bear Arete
beta: Begin out on the upper ledge's right-hand extremity and follow the right-hand arete of the highest summit. The face is overhanging, and the crux falls between bolts four and five.
overview: Follows the right-hand arete of the crag's highest summit, with sustained steep face climbing.

current.area_walk_in: Head up the fire road past the cliff, then take the narrow trail that doubles back through manzanita; allow 20 to 45 minutes from the road.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: at the extreme right of the upper terrace

name: Beast of Burden
beta: Technical moves matter more than strength here. Start on the crack's left side, clip three bolts, then step across the crack to the right for the final two bolts.
overview: Climbs five bolts alongside the line used to rappel down to the Yaks.

current.location: Same line as the abseil descent toward the Yaks

name: Beast of Burden
beta: Technical moves matter more than strength here. Start on the crack's left side, clip three bolts, then step across the crack to the right for the final two bolts.
overview: A five-star bolted line that asks for technique rather than raw power. It begins left of a crack and crosses over it near the top.

current.area_walk_in: Head up the fire road past the cliff, then take the narrow trail that doubles back through manzanita; allow 20 to 45 minutes from the road.

current.location: left of the crack

name: Beautiful Screamer
beta: Share the opening twenty feet with Beautiful Dreamer, then, stepping left, clip a bolt and pass three fixed pins before reaching the bolted rap station.
overview: Shares the first 20 ft with Beautiful Dreamer, then veers left, clipping one bolt and several pins on the way to the belay.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Bee Gees
beta: Four bolts protect the line; after the third, cut sharply rightward to gain the final one.
overview: Four bolts; after the third, the line cuts hard rightward to reach the final one.

current.area_walk_in: A path heading westward dwindles away at the foot of this big rock mass, whose northeast side can be spotted from far off. Routes here begin from a ledge high above the ground; easy scrambling up cracks below gets you onto it.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: leftmost line, starting from the high ledge

name: Bella Lugosi
beta: The crux comes right at the start: boulder up from the base to reach a crack tilting leftward that stops short of the ground. A single bolt sits near the top.
overview: A crack tilting leftward that hangs above the ground, gained by a bouldery start. A lone bolt guards the upper section, and the route was top-roped before its first lead.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Belly Dancer
beta: Start up a crack, then step rightward onto plates and climb past three bolts, although the third bolt appears to be absent.
overview: Starts in a crack on the detached tower, then trends right onto plate-like holds and bolts. The topmost bolt appears to be gone.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: freestanding tower beyond the western limit of Castle Rock; starts in a crack

name: Billabong
beta: Begin at the first bolt of the neighboring Shoveling Coal line and trend rightward past a pair of bolts, reaching a belay beneath a plated pillar. Ascend it to its top, traverse left along horizontal cracks, and finish up another crack.
overview: Shares its first bolt with Shovling Coal, then two more bolts lead rightward to a belay beneath a plated pillar. Over the pillar, traverse horizontal cracks leftward into another crack that finishes the route.

name: Bivvy Kitten
beta: Heading straight up to the first bolt is the harder way; starting from the left makes the opening easier. The route has two bolts.
overview: A short bolted face where moving directly to the opening bolt is tougher than angling in from the left; it was once a solo problem.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Black Hole Sun
beta: A finesse line where strength is unnecessary. Mono pockets appear on the way, though using them is optional, and six bolts lead to an anchor shared with another route.
overview: A finesse line where strength is not needed. Mono pockets appear along the way, handy but not required.

current.area_walk_in: Head up the fire road past the cliff, then take the narrow trail that doubles back through manzanita; allow 20 to 45 minutes from the road.

name: Black Lassie
beta: Climbing the right-hand crack system, a bolt about twenty feet up marks the spot to swap from the right-hand crack over into a left-hand one.
overview: A single bolt about 20 ft up marks where you move from the right crack to the left one.

current.area_walk_in: Roughly 500 yd eastward from the Creeper Rocks; one can stroll over from those formations.

name: Black Todd
beta: Step off a boulder and follow a sequence of cracks slanting rightward, clipping a bolt on the way and ending in one more rightward-slanting crack.
overview: Right-leaning cracks, past a bolt, to a final crack that also leans to the right.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Off a boulder immediately beyond the previous pair

name: Black Widow
beta: Opens on a brief crack and continues as face climbing past two bolts; a thorny cat's claw bush grows beside the start and must be negotiated.
overview: A two-bolt face whose lower section is a brief crack; a thorny bush sits at its foot and must be negotiated first.

name: Blast From the Past
beta: Bring large protection, as the offwidth and chimney take gear up to about six inches.

For the boulder routes, swing wide beyond Overbolted Rock keeping to its rightward flank, double back left, and scramble round the dome's northwest tip.

name: Souvenir
beta: Follow the barely formed crack upward, clipping two bolts on the way.
overview: A route tucked into the passage at the rear of the wall, following a faint crack with two bolts.

current.area_walk_in: Beyond the opening in the boulders above Zombie Woof, carry on fifty more yards; the wall sits to your right.

name: The Bat Cave
beta: From inside a large cave, the line moves onto overhanging rock with four bolts; carry a few natural pieces as well.
overview: Emerges from a large cave and goes up steeply leaning stone with four bolts.

name: Body Snatcher
beta: Reachy and mentally engaging, with a hard, dynamic crux just above the second bolt. Seven bolts lead to the anchor, and the stone here is volcanic tuff.
overview: A reachy route whose tough dynamic crux comes just past the second clip, on volcanic tuff.

name: Bolt Filcher
beta: A big high step and slapping between slopers carry you past the crux, found just beyond the third bolt.
overview: A highly rated bolted line whose difficulty is packed into a single sloper-heavy crux.

name: Bolt Route
beta:
The hardest climbing is low, from the ground to above the second bolt, and the base holds have been worn smooth on soft sandy rock.

Another tough move waits on your right once the final bolt is clipped; should you still have energy at the anchor, continue rightward up the upper bolts of Earthcling.
overview: A bolted face line. The hard part: lowest section up through bolt two, plus a tough move above the final bolt. Clip 13 bolts on the way up.

name: Bolt Route
beta: Easy ground leads up to bolt one, after which the route surmounts a steep bulge close beneath the top edge.
overview: A short bolted line with easy climbing early and its difficulty concentrated at an overhanging bulge.

beta: Begin among the bushes at the foot of the wall and work up the face next to Yucca Bowl; the bolts that once protected it are gone.

name: Brits In Drag
beta: Ascend the left-facing corner, then step rightward by a bolt to enter a finger crack that ends at a bolted belay. Shift right again to another bolt and finish up a crack.
overview: Climbs an open book, then shifts right, clipping a bolt, and enters a finger crack that ends at a bolted belay. Another step right gains a bolt; a crack above completes it.

overview: A faint right-facing book, with one bolt near its upper end.

beta: Begin on the gully-ledge that slopes rightward and upward, move left, then continue straight past the bolts.
overview: A bolted line that originally had three bolts, the first of which may now be missing.

name: Bubble Boy
beta: The hardest moves come between bolts one and three on juggy, steep rock. Veering left rather than right after the first clip makes the route noticeably easier.
overview: Steep but well supplied with big holds. A leftward deviation early on makes an easier 5.10d alternative.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Crystal Bonsai
beta: Once on Crystal Palace Ledge via the ramp, work up the dihedral all the way to its end, then trace the Crystal Corner leftward with bat hooks plus bolts to a two-bolt stance.
overview: Big-wall aid route up the tallest part of the wall, just left of center, tracing a white crystalline band running the full height.

current.approach: Walk east from Roads End on the Bubbs Creek trail, the same approach as for Charlotte Dome, to the good campsites just past Charlotte Creek. Continue down the trail a short way until the long wall comes into view on the left. The route follows the longest section of the wall, just left of centre, along a white crystal band. It starts at a big pine just up and right of the huge white left-facing dihedral that marks the foot of that band.
current.descent: From the top, descend west toward Charlotte Creek, the drainage that runs down toward Charlotte Dome, and follow it back to the Bubbs Creek trail.
current.detailed_rack: Tiny nuts up to 4 inches (two of each), one #5 Friend, one skyhook, two bathooks, two Leeper cam hooks, and hammocks.
current.location: Beside a big pine, roughly 100 yards uphill and rightward of the giant dihedral where the crystal band begins.
